name: Complex Numbers
strandNote: Desk quant: Fourier option pricing and characteristic functions.
description: Use numbers on a plane to turn rotations into multiplication and price options by Fourier inversion.

skills.cz-polar: The polar form and Euler’s formula

requires.why: Uses the compound angle formulae to see complex multiplication as rotation and prove De Moivre's theorem.
Derives e to the i theta from the Maclaurin series of exp, sin and cos.
Uses partial derivatives in the Cauchy-Riemann equations to test where a function is analytic.
Uses moment generating functions and densities of sums as the model for characteristic functions and Fourier inversion.

lessonNames.l1-square-root-of-minus-one: A square root of minus one
lessonNames.l2-points-in-a-plane: Numbers as points in a plane
lessonNames.l13-fourier-pricing: Pricing an option by Fourier inversion

lessonObjectives.l1-square-root-of-minus-one: Add, multiply and divide complex numbers, and solve a quadratic with no real roots.
lessonObjectives.l2-points-in-a-plane: Plot complex numbers, and read modulus, argument and conjugate from the plane.
lessonObjectives.l3-euler: Derive $e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta$ from series, and multiply by rotating.
lessonObjectives.l4-roots-of-unity: Find the $n$th roots of a complex number with De Moivre’s theorem.
lessonObjectives.l5-functions-move-the-plane: Picture a complex function as a map of the plane, using $z^2$ and $1/z$.
lessonObjectives.l6-complex-differentiability: Test whether a function has a complex derivative at a point.
lessonObjectives.l7-cauchy-riemann: Use the Cauchy-Riemann equations to decide where a function is analytic.
lessonObjectives.l8-exp-and-log: Work with the complex exponential and the many values of the logarithm.
lessonObjectives.l9-contour-integrals: Compute a contour integral by parametrising the path.
lessonObjectives.l10-cauchy-theorem: Use Cauchy’s theorem and integral formula to evaluate integrals around closed paths.
lessonObjectives.l11-residues: Evaluate a real integral by summing residues inside a contour.
lessonObjectives.l12-characteristic-functions: Find a distribution’s characteristic function and recover the density by Fourier inversion.
lessonObjectives.l13-fourier-pricing: Price a European call from the characteristic function of the log price, and match Black-Scholes in code.
